newsitem.title: THAILAND: PRESS DIGEST - Thai newspapers - June 24.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Thai newspapers - June 24.

text.p: These are some of the leading stories in the Thai press on Monday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.

- Chavalit "confirmed Pol Pot's arrest to Khmer co-Premiers'. The capture of Khmer Rouge leader Pol Pot by his former followers was confirmed by Prime Minister Chavalit Yongchaiyudh during his meeting with two prime ministers of Cambodia, a high-level army source said yesterday.

Cambodia's First Prime Minister Prince Norodom Ranariddh and Second Prime Minister Hun Sen jointly announced to the press in Phnom Penh on Saturday of Pol Pot's fate after the meeting with General Chavalit, source said. (BANGKOK POST)

- "Bravehaert" Thanong set for battle. The government yesterday declared it was armed and ready to meet opposition during the Budget Bill debate, while Prime Minister Chavalit Yongchaiyudh said the new finance minister was selected to lead the charge because of his "braveheart".

After returning from visiting Laos and Cambodia, Chavalit summoned Finance Minister Thanong Bidaya to a meeting with two deputy finance ministers and Budget Bureau officials to arm the new Cabinet member with information of defend himself against the opposition's onslaught. (The Nation)
- Help for small finance houses. Steps to manage small finance houses that are too weak to merge with others, and to ease market liquidity, are pending, according to Bank of Thailand officials.
These were confirmed by deputy governor Chaiyawat Wibulswasdi and Financial Institutions Development Fund managing director Swangchit Chaiyawat.
Ms Swangchit declined to elaborate as the details had yet to be looked at by new Finance Minister Thanong Bidaya. (Post Business)

- 2-tier market seen as key to stability. The two-tier foreign exchange market, which is expected to remain in place for a while, will provide the country with the best opportunity to consolidate its economic fundamentals and money market, according to Citibank.
During the "Bourse Game" seminar held on June 16 to 20, Citibank presened a positive outlook on the stability of the Thai baht to the bank's customers. (The Nation Business)
